title: For All Beings
ordering: Editorial: compassion and accessible practice first, then more contextual teachings. Not an objective ranking of spiritual efficacy.

teachings.author: Yeshe Tsogyal (traditional attribution; Pema Lingpa terma)
teachings.quote: May any connection we have be of deepest benefit and meaning.
teachings.locator: Bodhicitta stanza, last line ('dreltsé dön dang denpar shok')
teachings.context_note: Aspiration to benefit beings through every connection; attributed speech preserved in a later treasure revelation.

teachings.author: Seung Sahn
teachings.quote: Open your mouth and it's already a mistake. But our job is to help all beings.
teachings.locator: Paragraph beginning 'So, already everybody has dharma'
teachings.translator: English teaching as published by Kwan Um School; no translator credited
teachings.context_note: Paradox about speech and transmission immediately resolved through teaching for others' benefit.

teachings.author: Ajahn Chah
teachings.quote: Practice by letting go. Don’t hold on. Or if you hold on, don’t hold on tight.
teachings.locator: Putting Down the Glass, opening three sentences
teachings.translator: Thanissaro Bhikkhu, revised edition, introduction May 2013
teachings.context_note: Holding provisionally to investigate then setting down; not indifference.

teachings.author: Somā
teachings.quote: What difference does being a woman make when the mind's well-centered, when knowledge is progressing, seeing clearly, rightly, into the Dhamma.
teachings.locator: Somā’s first response verse to Māra
teachings.context_note: The nun refutes Māra’s claim that women cannot attain.

teachings.author: Attributed to Padmasambhava
teachings.quote:
My view is higher than the sky,
My attention to the karmic process finer than grains of flour.
teachings.work: My view is higher than the sky…
teachings.locator: Complete couplet
teachings.context_note: Source explicitly labels attribution; ultimate view coupled with karmic care.

teachings.author: Mipham
teachings.quote:
Teaching is not paramount, meditation is.
When meditating don’t teach but learn deeply.
To teach without meditating is to be like a parrot.
teachings.locator: Concluding verse first three lines
teachings.context_note: Emphasizes analytical practice, not anti-intellectualism.

teachings.author: Shikai Zuiko
teachings.quote:
When you notice anything whatsoever,
notice everything else that’s going on
without naming it.
teachings.work: Wherever You Stand 9: Who: Dajian Huineng Part 2
teachings.locator: Instructions after striking floor, lines beginning When you notice
teachings.context_note: Actual speaker is modern teacher Shikai Zuiko, not Huineng whom talk discusses.

teachings.author: Patrul Rinpoche
teachings.quote: Mind has always been empty. There is no need to search. It is the very one who searches.
teachings.locator: Opening instructions, paragraph beginning 'You won’t find the mind'
teachings.context_note: Opening instructions identify the searcher itself as mind; surrounding passage instructs settling without distraction.

teachings.author: Tilopa
teachings.quote: When you attain non-attainment, you attain Mahāmudrā.
teachings.locator: §19, final sentence
teachings.translator: Ina Bieler; edited by Kay Candler; revised 2023
teachings.context_note: Final line of verse 19, following retreat and non-meditation instructions; Tilopa addresses Naropa.

teachings.author: Avalokiteśvara in the Heart Sūtra
teachings.quote: Form is empty; emptiness is form. Emptiness is not other than form; form is not other than emptiness.
teachings.locator: Avalokiteśvara’s reply to Śāriputra, first paragraph
teachings.context_note: Actual speaker Avalokiteśvara, teaching through Buddha’s power.

teachings.author: Longchen Rabjam
teachings.quote:
Phenomena in their variety are like reflections in a mirror:
Appearing yet empty—and there’s no emptiness but this.
teachings.locator: Stanza beginning 'Phenomena in their variety', first two lines
teachings.context_note: Appearance and emptiness presented inseparably; subsequent lines advise certainty rather than naive reification.

teachings.author: Sera Khandro
teachings.quote:
Nothing truly exists.
Everything is empty.
Nothing is non-existent.
Everything is very clear.
teachings.work: I Don’t Believe in Samsara… Spiritual Advice
teachings.locator: Four lines beginning Nothing truly exists
teachings.context_note: Emptiness paired with clarity, avoiding nihilistic truncation.

teachings.author: Dōgen
teachings.quote: No trace of realization remains, and this no-trace continues endlessly.
teachings.locator: p. 1, paragraph beginning To study the buddha way, final sentence
teachings.translator: Robert Aitken and Kazuaki Tanahashi; revised at San Francisco Zen Center
teachings.context_note: Forgetting self and actualization by myriad things; continuing practice.

teachings.author: Śāntideva
teachings.quote:
When neither entity nor non-entity
Remain before the mind,
There is no position left to take,
And it rests in non-conceptual peace.
teachings.work: Bodhicaryāvatāra 9.34, quoted in Khenpo Petsé’s Meditation on the Great Middle Way
teachings.locator: Examining the Essence of Phenomena, quotation at note 15
teachings.translator: Cortland Dahl under Khenpo Sherab Sangpo, 2007; Lotsawa House 2022
teachings.context_note: After analysis of dependent arising; contextual sequel connects insight to compassion.

teachings.author: Mipham Rinpoche
teachings.quote: The actual nature of things is inconceivable and inexpressible.
teachings.locator: Opening sentence
teachings.context_note: Opening statement followed by illustrative instructions; not a rejection of teaching or practice.

teachings.author: Rongzom Chökyi Zangpo
teachings.quote: We only repudiate your inferior metaphysical views without establishing any superior point of our own.
teachings.locator: Final paragraph, response to What, then, does your tradition establish?
teachings.context_note: Polemical response within vehicle classification, rejecting a metaphysical thesis of one’s own.

teachings.author: The Buddha
teachings.quote: When there is no you there, you are neither here nor yonder nor between the two.
teachings.locator: Final instruction to Bāhiya, paragraph beginning 'When for you'
teachings.translator: Thanissaro Bhikkhu, 1994; Access to Insight edition 2012
teachings.context_note: Excerpt from the Buddha’s instruction to Bāhiya concerning seeing, hearing, sensing and cognizing without identification.

teachings.author: The Buddha
teachings.quote: There is, monks, an unborn — unbecome — unmade — unfabricated.
teachings.locator: First sentence of inspired utterance
teachings.context_note: Unconditioned as escape from the conditioned.

teachings.author: The Buddha
teachings.quote: And there, I say, there is neither coming, nor going, nor staying; neither passing away nor arising: unestablished, unevolving, without support [mental object].
teachings.locator: Inspired utterance second sentence, before This, just this...
teachings.context_note: Description of unbinding; bracketed phrase is translator’s wording; footnote markers omitted.

teachings.author: Padmasambhava (attributed)
teachings.quote:
Unstained by objects of perception,
Unspoilt by apprehending thought,
Sustaining naked, empty awareness—
This is the wisdom of all the buddhas!
teachings.locator: Four-line quotation; reported pure vision of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo
teachings.context_note: Source attributes these words to Padmasambhava in a pure vision of Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo; not represented as a historical transcript.

teachings.author: Dudjom Lingpa
teachings.quote:
Settle without holding to a technique. Be done with that.
Just relax—at ease—letting go of distraction and meditation.
teachings.work: Meditation Advice to the Nun Chötso
teachings.locator: Third stanza, first two lines
teachings.translator: Ringu Tulku and Holly Gayley, 2018; revised 2022
teachings.context_note: Advice for an experienced meditator; the conclusion explicitly preserves ethical discernment.

teachings.author: Sera Khandro
teachings.quote:
Alpha-pure, inexpressible awareness,
Beyond colour and characteristics—
Carefully analyze with intelligence.
Demolish the “I” or self at its source.
teachings.locator: Four-line abecedarian poem
teachings.context_note: The 'I' means self-grasping; Tibetan alphabet acrostic rendered in English abecedarian form.

teachings.author: Third Karmapa, Rangjung Dorje
teachings.quote:
Mind itself is without mind, empty of mind’s essence—
Empty yet unrestricted, appearing in any way at all.
teachings.work: Aspiration of the Mahāmudrā of Definitive Meaning
teachings.locator: Stanza beginning All phenomena, lines 2–3
teachings.context_note: Emptiness and unobstructed appearance together, not a claim of nonexistence.

teachings.author: Longchen Rabjam
teachings.quote:
In naturally arisen awareness, boundless and unconfined,
Undo the knot that retains the aspects of ordinary mind.
teachings.locator: Concluding dedication, first two lines
teachings.context_note: Concluding verse of Dzogchen instructions; text marked for transmission holders, excerpt is a general concluding aspiration.

teachings.author: Padampa Sangye, quoted by Dodrupchen
teachings.quote:
We human beings can cope with a lot of suffering,
But very little happiness.
teachings.work: Transforming Suffering and Happiness into Enlightenment
teachings.locator: Section 2.i, quotation attributed to Padampa Sangye
teachings.translator: Adam Pearcey, 2006, based on Rigpa Translations
teachings.context_note: Warns about complacency when happy; text teaches use of both happiness and suffering.

teachings.author: Rongzom Chökyi Zangpo
teachings.quote: Distinction between continuums of self and other, moreover, are divided in and by persons; they are not qualitatively different phenomena.
teachings.locator: Penultimate argument, paragraph beginning 'The eightfold assemblage'
teachings.context_note: Argument concerning consciousness and the divinity of appearances; source grammar preserved.

teachings.author: Marpa Lotsāwa
teachings.quote:
This mental consciousness, reifying what is internal,
Is realized to be unborn dharmakāya.
teachings.work: Song quoted in Mahāmudrā Way of Resting by Fifth Shamarpa
teachings.locator: Quotation introduced 'Lord Marpa sang', final two lines; note 15
teachings.context_note: Marpa summarizes Maitripa's instructions; quoted by Fifth Shamarpa, not misattributed to him.

teachings.author: Nāropa
teachings.quote:
When you discover the taste of co-emergence,
Saṃsāra is overwhelmed, transformed into great bliss.
teachings.work: A Spiritual Song on the Eight Supreme Difficulties
teachings.locator: First appended gaṇacakra verse, last two lines
teachings.context_note: A song attributed to Nāropa preserved in Marpa’s collected works vol1 p76.

teachings.author: Padmasambhava in Pema Ledrel Tsal’s terma
teachings.quote: Tsogyal, there are many who claim to have realized emptiness, but few who have realized the ultimate nature.
teachings.work: The Golden Garland of Nectar: Questions and Answers
teachings.locator: Essence, Nature and Compassion, section 1 Essence, final sentence
teachings.context_note: Dialogue warns against sterile emptiness and abandoning compassion; treasure attribution, not historical transcript.

teachings.author: Attributed to Milarepa
teachings.quote:
Capturing the fortress of the deathless unending nature of mind.
Now all fear of death is over and done.
teachings.locator: Final two lines
teachings.translator: Rigpa Translations; version on Lotsawa House verified 2026-09-28
teachings.context_note: Preceding lines describe retreat and repeated contemplation of uncertain death; not a claim of bodily immortality.

teachings.author: Man Gong
teachings.quote: You and I are not two, not one. Only your stupid thinking is nonstop.
teachings.work: Prajna Ship, quoted in Pilgrimage to India, 2011
teachings.locator: Block quotation introduced as Man Gong’s Prajna Ship; middle two sentences
teachings.translator: Kwan Um School English version; translator uncredited
teachings.context_note: Article explains not attaching to thinking, rather than eliminating the thinking mind.

teachings.author: Nāgārjuna (traditional attribution)
teachings.quote:
I bow to all dharmakāyas abiding
At the eight stūpas of Śākyamuni,
In the ten directions, and elsewhere—
I humbly pay homage, always, to peace!
teachings.work: In Praise of the Stūpas at the Eight Great Sacred Places
teachings.locator: Ninth stanza
teachings.translator: Monica Thunder and Peter Woods, Samye Translations; v1.0–20230907
teachings.context_note: Traditional Tengyur attribution, Toh 1133, Derge vol1 fol81b3–82a3. Homage to peace.

teachings.author: Padmasambhava (Dorje Lingpa treasure attribution)
teachings.quote: The most vital point is therefore to sustain your practice undistractedly from this very moment.
teachings.work: The Final Words of Padmasambhava / Sacred Refined Essence Instruction; included in Dakini Teachings
teachings.locator: Standalone paragraph beginning “The most vital point”, following the paragraph defining the innate deity
teachings.context_note: Instruction to Yeshe Tsogyal on practice, death and the bardo; traditional treasure attribution to Padmasambhava, revealed by Dorje Lingpa. Article credited to the translator; colophon explicitly credits his translation. No independent historical-transcript claim.
teachings.source_use_note: One short 16-word excerpt recorded from this work; check cumulative work-level use before further excerpts.

teachings.author: The Buddha (canonical attribution)
teachings.quote: For hatred does not cease by hatred at any time: hatred ceases by love, this is an old rule.
teachings.locator: Verse 5
teachings.context_note: Complete numbered verse checked with neighboring verses in the source. Historical translation; retain its wording without modernization. Mix sparingly with the prioritized Tibetan translations rather than publish as a continuous book sequence.
teachings.edition: The Sacred Books of the East, Volume X, Part I; Project Gutenberg eBook 2017 transcription
teachings.rights: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg catalog; not a claim about every jurisdiction.

teachings.author: The Buddha (canonical attribution)
teachings.quote: As the bee collects nectar and departs without injuring the flower, or its colour or scent, so let a sage dwell in his village.
teachings.locator: Verse 49
teachings.context_note: Complete numbered verse checked with neighboring verses in the source. Historical translation; retain its wording without modernization. Mix sparingly with the prioritized Tibetan translations rather than publish as a continuous book sequence.
teachings.edition: The Sacred Books of the East, Volume X, Part I; Project Gutenberg eBook 2017 transcription
teachings.rights: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg catalog; not a claim about every jurisdiction.

teachings.author: The Buddha (canonical attribution)
teachings.quote: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise.
teachings.locator: Verse 81
teachings.context_note: Complete numbered verse checked with neighboring verses in the source. Historical translation; retain its wording without modernization. Mix sparingly with the prioritized Tibetan translations rather than publish as a continuous book sequence.
teachings.edition: The Sacred Books of the East, Volume X, Part I; Project Gutenberg eBook 2017 transcription
teachings.rights: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg catalog; not a claim about every jurisdiction.

teachings.author: The Buddha (canonical attribution)
teachings.quote: Wise people, after they have listened to the laws, become serene, like a deep, smooth, and still lake.
teachings.locator: Verse 82
teachings.context_note: Complete numbered verse checked with neighboring verses in the source. Historical translation; retain its wording without modernization. Mix sparingly with the prioritized Tibetan translations rather than publish as a continuous book sequence.
teachings.edition: The Sacred Books of the East, Volume X, Part I; Project Gutenberg eBook 2017 transcription
teachings.rights: Public domain in the USA per Project Gutenberg catalog; not a claim about every jurisdiction.

teachings.author: Gampopa (as presented by Erik Pema Kunsang)
teachings.quote: Don’t reject compassion, since it is the basis for helping others.
teachings.locator: First bullet of the eleven instructions
teachings.translator: Erik Pema Kunsang (English presentation; no separate translation credit on page)
teachings.context_note: Article explicitly attributes the list to Gampopa. This compassion instruction is self-contained. Article author is Erik Pema Kunsang; credit the presentation rather than invent a separate edition or translation colophon.
teachings.source_use_note: One brief excerpt from this work recorded in this batch; retain cumulative work-level use tracking.

teachings.author: Tsoknyi Rinpoche
teachings.quote: Someone who has realized emptiness is naturally compassionate, and doesn’t close off and become concerned with only him or herself.
teachings.locator: Paragraph beginning “Even though he was not quite up to doing so”; sentence beginning “Someone who has realized emptiness”
teachings.translator: Erik Pema Kunsang and Marcia Binder Schmidt; edited by Kerry Moran
teachings.context_note: Tsoknyi Rinpoche speaking about the example of his father Tulku Urgyen. Actual speaker is Tsoknyi, not Tulku Urgyen or the article byline. Colophon credits translators, editor, and 1998 copyright.
teachings.source_use_note: One brief excerpt from this work recorded in this batch; retain cumulative work-level use tracking.

teachings.author: Nyoshul Khen Rinpoche
teachings.quote: Let unmoved mind look into itself.
teachings.work: The Perfect Mirror (poem in Erik Pema Kunsang’s article)
teachings.locator: Revised translation of the poem; final line of stanza beginning “See here, friends of the unchanging!”
teachings.context_note: Kunsang explicitly introduces this as his new translation of Nyoshul Khenpo’s poem. This line is from the poem, not the translator’s surrounding commentary; nondual presence is the stated context.
teachings.source_use_note: One brief excerpt from this work recorded in this batch; retain cumulative work-level use tracking.

teachings.author: Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche
teachings.quote: Emptiness without compassion is never taught to be the true path of enlightenment.
teachings.locator: Final teaching paragraph, second sentence
teachings.translator: Erik Pema Kunsang (editor credited; separate translator not specified on page)
teachings.context_note: Oral teaching excerpt introduced as Tulku Urgyen; compassion and emptiness as inseparable. Article notes partial extraction from Treasures from Juniper Ridge; track that work cumulatively. Not a recording.
teachings.attribution_status: Teaching attributed to Tulku Urgyen by editor

teachings.author: Sera Khandro
teachings.quote: In your behavior, love beings from all six realms as your own children.
teachings.locator: Line beginning In your behavior, immediately before The ground is to stabilize bodhicitta
teachings.context_note: Advice joins conduct, bodhicitta, meditation and action/results; direct authorial advice.
teachings.edition: Lotsawa House version 1.2–20220818; Tibetan collected works vol.5 pp.203–204

teachings.author: Muttā (canonical attribution)
teachings.quote: Having uprooted the craving that leads to becoming, I'm set free from aging & death.
teachings.locator: I.11 — Mutta, final sentence
teachings.context_note: The nun celebrates freedom after describing release from domestic drudgery. This is her own first-person verse, not advice addressed to her.

teachings.author: Avalokiteśvara (speaker in the sūtra)
teachings.quote: Form is empty. Emptiness is form. Emptiness is not other than form, and form is also not other than emptiness.
teachings.work: The Heart of the Perfection of Wisdom, the Blessed Mother (Toh 21)
teachings.locator: Section 1.6; Avalokiteśvara’s answer to Śāriputra
teachings.translator: Dharmachakra Translation Committee; translation produced by Catherine Dalton and Andreas Doctor
teachings.context_note: Avalokiteśvara explains the five aggregates’ lack of intrinsic nature in answer to Śāriputra’s question about practicing the perfection of wisdom. Actual speaker is Avalokiteśvara, not the Buddha.
teachings.rights: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; unchanged attributed excerpt for noncommercial use. Software remains separately MIT-licensed.

teachings.author: Sela (canonical attribution)
teachings.quote: This doll isn't self-made, nor is this misery made by another. In dependence on a cause it comes into play. With the dissolution of the cause it ceases.
teachings.locator: Sela’s reply to Māra, verse after “she replied to him in verses”
teachings.context_note: After recognizing Māra’s challenge about who made the “doll,” the nun Sela answers that the aggregates arise dependent on causes and cease when those causes dissolve. These are Sela’s words, not Māra’s.
teachings.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0; brief unchanged attributed excerpt, no more than 28 words from this work.

teachings.author: Ārya Nāgārjuna
teachings.quote:
In this, there is not a thing to be removed,
Nor the slightest thing to be added.
It is looking perfectly into reality itself,
And when reality is seen, complete liberation.
teachings.work: The Heart of Dependent Origination, verse 7
teachings.locator: Verse 7, four lines; Derge Tengyur Toḥ 1135 vol.96 146b.2–7
teachings.context_note: The verse describes seeing reality itself, not a thing to add or remove; retained as a single verse.
teachings.rights: CC BY-NC 4.0; brief attributed noncommercial excerpt. Translation wording retained unchanged.

teachings.author: Zen Master Dae Kwang
teachings.quote: It was not to solve some intellectual puzzle, or even to take away his own suffering. Rather, it was for all beings.
teachings.work: Why does the Buddha have big ears?
teachings.locator: Paragraph 5, final two sentences
teachings.translator: No translator credited; original English teaching
teachings.context_note: Dae Kwang explains the Buddha’s search as directed toward the welfare of all beings rather than solving an intellectual puzzle or ending only his own suffering.
teachings.rights: Brief attributed excerpt from the official Kwan Um School of Zen teaching archive; no separate open-license claim.

teachings.author: Somā (nun speaking to Māra)
teachings.quote:
What difference does womanhood make
when the mind is serene,
and knowledge is present
as you rightly discern the Dhamma.
teachings.locator: SN 5.2, verse 4; Somā replies to Māra.
teachings.context_note: Somā rejects Māra’s sexist challenge: gender is irrelevant when the mind is serene and one rightly discerns Dhamma.
teachings.rights: SuttaCentral translation released CC0 per SuttaCentral source record.

teachings.author: Kathy Park JDPSN
teachings.quote: Listen to your partners. Listen to your children. Listen to your coworkers you don't like.
teachings.work: Listen with Intention, Hear with Compassion
teachings.locator: Final paragraph, sentence urging attention to disliked coworkers.
teachings.translator: No translator credited; original English teaching
teachings.context_note: Within a teaching on listening to the world’s suffering, Kathy Park urges compassionate attention even to coworkers one dislikes.
teachings.rights: Brief attributed excerpt from official source; no open license asserted.

teachings.author: Sera Khandro
teachings.quote: Recite and spread the six syllables to benefit yourself and others.
teachings.locator: Lines 65–66; Tibetan edition BDRC W1PD108254 vol. 5, pp. 203–204.
teachings.context_note: The line completes a short instruction to share the six syllables for the benefit of oneself and others; distinct from the other excerpt from this work already in the archive.
teachings.rights: Lotsawa House CC BY-NC 4.0; brief attributed noncommercial excerpt.

teachings.author: Candrakīrti
teachings.quote: Love is the seed of this abundant harvest of buddhahood.
teachings.locator: Chapter 1, verse 2, first line.
teachings.context_note: The opening line of verse 2. The complete verse develops compassion as the seed and water that bring the harvest of buddhahood to fruition; this self-contained first sentence is exact and unstitched.
teachings.rights: Lotsawa House CC BY-NC 4.0; brief attributed noncommercial excerpt.

teachings.author: Padmasambhava (treasure text recorded by Yeshe Tsogyal; revealed by Dorje Lingpa)
teachings.quote: To remain undistracted in the state of stillness, without fabrication or fixation, that is the meditation.
teachings.work: The Final Words of Padmasambhava / Sacred Refined Essence Instruction
teachings.locator: Reply to Yeshe Tsogyal, paragraph defining meditation, lines 16–17.
teachings.translator: Erik Pema Kunsang; translated according to oral instructions of Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche and Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche
teachings.context_note: Within the treasure narrative, the master defines view, meditation and conduct after describing the nature of mind. This complete sentence defines meditation.
teachings.rights: Brief excerpt from copyrighted translation; full credit and direct source link included.
